narratives.text: The engineering director should run a short practice review with Phoenix on what changed in testing, review and release habits since week 5. Publish the findings and share them with Atlas, where quality is deteriorating. Success by week 22 means Phoenix keeps its gains and adopting teams stop deteriorating; a medium priority suits knowledge sharing rather than an urgent fix.

narratives.author: risk-narrator
narratives.text: Atlas quality is deteriorating: test coverage fell from 72% to 63.2% and automated tests from 80.4% to 75.7% since week 8, while defects rose from 6 to 12 and rework rate from 8.3% to 12.8%. More defects may reach users, and more unplanned rework competes with roadmap work. One possibility worth checking is whether falling coverage and automated tests are associated with the defect rise, as coverage changes preceded defect changes by 1 week; this association does not establish causality and is shown only as a possibility.

narratives.author: risk-narrator
narratives.text: Reliability on the Data platform is deteriorating: change failure rate rose from 5.4% to 27.1%, rollback rate from 1.1% to 25.9%, failed deployments from 0.5 to 6 and incidents from 1 to 5.5. This may mean more failed releases and customer-facing incidents on the affected services. One possibility is deployment-related changes, as incidents attributed to a change in post-incident reviews went from 50% to 80%; the caveat is that this shift is not statistically significant (p=0.097).
